Patient demographics:
  age: 38
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: North American
  relationship_status: In a relationship
  occupation: Bartender
  trauma_type: Trauma to a loved one
  pcl5: 38

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid News: News reports about events similar to what happened to me, Emotion Control: I try hard to control my emotions, Avoid Medical Care: Seeking medical or psychological help
  Memory: Vivid Memory: My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed., Partial Clarity: Some moments of the event are extremely clear while others are completely blank, Visual Memories: My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images.
  Negative Appraisals: Self-Blame: The event happened because of the way I acted, Distrust Others: People are not what they seem, Can't Rely on Others: I can't rely on other people

Vignette:
Samantha had always been a social person, thriving in her role as a bartender where she got to meet new people every day. But that all changed two years ago when her younger brother was involved in a tragic accident at a music festival, where a stage collapsed and several people were killed. Samantha's brother was one of the lucky ones who survived, but he suffered severe injuries that left him with permanent brain damage. Samantha was consumed by guilt and self-blame after the incident. She couldn't shake off the feeling that if she had been more responsible and looked out for her brother better, this wouldn't have happened. Her memories of that day were vivid and clear - she remembered every detail of the frantic phone calls to the hospital, the agonizing wait in the emergency room, and the devastating news that followed. As time went on, Samantha found it increasingly difficult to cope with her emotions. She tried hard to control them, putting on a brave face for her brother's sake as well as her own. But inside, she was torn apart by feelings of anger, sadness, and helplessness. She became withdrawn and isolated, avoiding social gatherings and events that might trigger memories of the accident. Samantha also started to avoid news reports about similar incidents, fearing that they would bring back painful memories. When a recent stage collapse at a concert made headlines, she couldn't bear to watch the news or scroll through her social media feeds. Her partner tried to reassure her, but she pushed him away, feeling like he just didn't understand. Samantha's distrust of others grew over time. She became convinced that people were not what they seemed, and that even those closest to her might be hiding secrets. She started to question her own relationships, wondering if anyone was truly looking out for her brother's well-being or if it was all just a facade. Her fear of relying on others made her feel like she had to handle everything alone. Despite her struggles, Samantha continued to work as a bartender, but she found it increasingly difficult to connect with customers and colleagues. She felt like she was living in a world where tragedy could strike at any moment, and that no one was truly safe. When regulars asked about her brother or how she was doing, she brushed them off, afraid of breaking down in front of strangers. Seeking medical or psychological help seemed like an admission of weakness to Samantha. She didn't want to be a burden on others, and besides, what could anyone do to fix the unfixable? Her partner encouraged her to seek therapy, but she refused, convinced that she just needed to toughen up and move on. It wasn't until Samantha had a panic attack at work, in front of a packed bar, that she realized she couldn't keep living like this. She was exhausted from trying to control her emotions, and the fear of losing herself completely was starting to outweigh her fear of seeking help. As she sat in her dimly lit apartment, surrounded by the silence of her avoidance, Samantha knew it was time to face her demons head-on. With a mix of trepidation and hope, she picked up the phone and made an appointment with a therapist, praying that someone could finally help her find a way out of this darkness.
